merge_group continues to run the full medium tier unchanged, so an under-selection delays detection without allowing a regression to merge.
Selection reuses scripts/canary_impact.py with a parameterised marker expression and CANT_AFFECT list; no second selector or coverage-based tool is introduced.
Any test whose dependency closure contains an unresolved library import is always selected, with a changed-path selection test pinning the benchbox/monitoring lazy-export case.
read_holder decodes best effort; both wait loops retry only platform-documented contention errors, covered by a contended Windows-path test.

BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS defaults to 3600 locally and 0 in every workflow that runs pytest; tests/conftest.py, the BLOCKED message, tests/README.md and docs/operations/dev-loop-worktrees.md all match the new default.

description:
The local preflight runs the full medium tier for every code-routed diff: 2113 tests, 6m13s on an idle 10-core machine, and 9m53s with a timeout failure under concurrent load. With 10-12 concurrent agent sessions sharing that machine there is under one core per session, so this tier is the dominant local cost and the source of global test-lock contention.

The cost arrived in two steps. PR #2171 added `make test-medium` to `pr-preflight` for `needs-code-ci` diffs; PR #2180 then removed the heavy tier from `pull_request` CI and left it on `merge_group`. Path classification is coarse - `scripts/path_filter_decision.py` emits four buckets - so a diff of documentation, one workflow, one test file and a Makefile comment pulls all 2113 tests.

Replace the full tier in the local preflight with an impact-selected subset. Keep CI placement exactly as it is: `merge_group` continues to run the full medium tier (.github/workflows/pr.yml:685,706). That is what makes an under-selection a detection-latency cost rather than a correctness one - nothing merges without the full tier, so selection needs no observation window before it is trusted.

Prior art: `scripts/canary_impact.py` on branch `fix/canary-impact-selector` already maps changed paths to affected tests for the release canary, with transitive import closure including parent package initializers, importlib literals, REPO_ROOT and __file__ path edges with directory expansion, conftest chains and pytest_plugins, and fail-safe whole-suite fallbacks for configuration, lockfile and selector changes. Extend it by parameterising its marker expression and CANT_AFFECT list. Do not write a second selector.

Cover the known lazy-export gap by always selecting any test whose dependency closure contains an unresolved library import. `benchbox/monitoring/__init__.py:45` resolves exports through `__getattr__` and `importlib.import_module(f"{__name__}.{module_name}")`, a computed name the selector cannot resolve, so `tests/unit/monitoring/test_resource_monitoring.py` would otherwise be missed when its backing module changes.

Ship alongside the test-lock defects the same contention exposed. `read_holder` (scripts/local_validation.py:124) catches only OSError, so a lock file containing invalid UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError out of `wait_on_fd`, which reads holder text before attempting the lock. Both wait loops retry every OSError as contention; this must become platform-specific, BlockingIOError on POSIX and the documented OSError from `msvcrt.locking(LK_NBLCK)` on Windows. `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS` defaults to 0 (tests/conftest.py:105), leaving the existing bounded waiter in `wait_on_fd` unreachable and turning momentary contention into a hard stop; default it to 3600 to match the receipt-lock budget while CI pins it to 0.

Rejected, with reasons: shadow mode and an observation window as a promotion gate, because merge_group already provides the backstop; selecting tests in PR or merge_group CI; scheduled medium runs; ticket files, queue daemons and counting semaphores, because flock is released by the kernel on process death and carries no stale-state recovery burden; age-biased polling; a second xdist worker cap, because `_benchbox_pytest_xdist_safety.py` already caps auto to 5 on a 10-core machine; coverage-based selectors such as pytest-testmon, which would be a second selection mechanism; and making heavy `-n 0` lanes take the global lock, which adds serialization to a machine whose problem is total work.
